clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old Nigerian female presented with recurrent headache, fever, easy fatiguability, and breathlessness of 2 months duration, with a history of prior treatment for typhoid/malaria and 3 units of blood transfusion for anemia. Physical examination revealed severe pallor and slight jaundice. Initial workup showed pancytopenia (PCV 10.8, WBC 4.1 x 10^9/L, platelet 50 x 10^9/L). Peripheral blood film revealed immature mononuclear cells with cytoplasmic blebs and giant platelets. Bone marrow aspiration yielded a dry tap, but imprint showed over 90% immature mononuclear cells with cytoplasmic blebs. Immunophenotyping of peripheral blood confirmed AML, M7 subtype, with positivity for CD33, CD41, and CD61. X-rays of tibia and fibula showed increased fibrosis. Induction therapy was initiated with cytarabine and daunorubicin (7+3 regimen). On day 7 of induction, repeat FBC showed leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and no abnormal mononuclear cells, and a repeat bone marrow aspiration showed blasts less than 5%, indicating remission.
